input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled)
input.rationale: Section 6.1 imposes a non-compete/field-of-use restriction on our client (the Company), barring it from participating in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or products "substantially similar" to them — expressly including competitor product lines. That sweeps in our other e-commerce channels, brands and sourcing decisions, contrary to the playbook position that we accept no restrictions on the businesses we operate or the products we buy or build. The only carve-out (Section 6.2, closeout merchandise) is far narrower than needed. The reciprocal restriction on HDI in Section 6.3 is acceptable and left untouched. Preferred redline deletes the Company-side covenant while preserving HDI's exclusive right to the "Deerskin" branded site (the core bargain); the comment offers the fallback of a restriction limited to Deerskin Products, term-only, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the covenant barring the Company from participating in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or "substantially similar" products, as we cannot accept restrictions on the channels we operate or the products we source or build; HDI's exclusive right to the "Deerskin" branded site is preserved. If HDI needs protection, we can accept a fallback limited to Deerskin Products only, during the term, with carve-outs for our internal development and acquired businesses.
proposal.summary: Delete the non-compete/field-of-use restriction on the Company in Section 6.1, retaining HDI's brand exclusivity for the Site.
